title: Mara and the Harbor
premise: In 1893, Mirabel Lockridge keeps the light at Grayharbor Point, a widower who has spent three years making himself small enough that the Admiralty forgets he exists. When winter storms close the causeway bridge and a shipwreck washes a dying man ashore carrying papers that prove the Admiralty scuttled its own vessel for insurance, Mirabel must choose between the safe silence that has kept him fed and the record that might save the wreck's surviving crew from blame. Trapped on the point until spring thaw, sheltering the man's daughter and the harbor's outcasts in his tower, he finds the family he thought he'd lost — and learns that survival bought with invisibility is its own kind of drowning. The book ends in April, when the bridge reopens and the victors' historians arrive: Mirabel gets the truth notarized and into a journalist's hands hours before they do, at the cost of his post, his pension, and his anonymity — but not, at last, of his name.
about_author: Gideon Crane is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing lighthouse logs and Admiralty inquiry records along the northern coast. This is their third novel, written in a keeper's cottage rented through one full storm season.

chapters.title: The Arithmetic of Light
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Establishes his routines, his ledger-keeping mind, and his late wife Ede's chair still by the window. He trims wicks, logs weather, and counts what he owns in things that can be carried. Emotional beat: grief worn smooth into habit, and the first hint that the Admiralty's autumn inspection is coming early.

chapters.title: Orders, Signed and Sealed
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The annual supply boat brings a sealed directive: the causeway bridge will close for the season ahead of schedule, and an Admiralty vessel, the Corvus, will pass the point in November. The harbormaster's clerk, a sharp-eyed woman named Tamsin Vole, lingers, uneasy. Emotional beat: dread disguised as paperwork; Mirabel decides to be invisible.

chapters.title: The Corvus Comes In
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, night watch. In the worst gale in a decade, the Corvus founders on the shoal within sight of his lamp — a wreck he swears he lit for. He launches his skiff and pulls one survivor, a badly burned man clutching a satchel. Emotional beat: guilt igniting into purpose; the first crack in his invisibility.

chapters.title: What the Drowned Man Carried
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The survivor, stoker Elias Brand, dies at dawn but not before pressing the satchel on him: manifests proving the Corvus was overloaded and deliberately scuttled for insurance, with the inquiry already rigged. Emotional beat: the terrible weight of being the only witness; Mirabel wants to burn it all.

chapters.title: A Girl on the Rocks
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, then brief shift to the girl's. Days later he finds Brand's daughter, Nell, sixteen, searching the shoreline for her father. He cannot turn her out into the closed season. Emotional beat: reluctant shelter becoming something warmer; Ede's chair finally gets an occupant.

chapters.title: The Harbor's Leftovers
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV through Mirabel's eyes. The stranded gather at the tower: Tamsin the clerk, a disgraced ship's cook, an old pilot who once ran contraband. Mirabel feeds them from his winter stores and hates how much he doesn't hate it. Emotional beat: found family assembling without anyone admitting it.

chapters.title: The First Boat of Inquiry
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. An Admiralty launch braves the storm to 'recover effects' — actually hunting Brand and the satchel. Mirabel lies smoothly for the first time in his life and realizes how good he's gotten at disappearing things. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into craft; the stakes become personal.

chapters.title: Nell's Testimony
chapters.summary: Nell's POV. She reads her father's letters and realizes he'd written to her about the overloading weeks before the wreck — corroboration Mirabel never had. She demands to be part of getting it on record. Emotional beat: rage transmuted into resolve; Mirabel's guilt meets her grief and neither flinches.

chapters.title: Ledgers and Lanterns
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. He and Tamsin, who keeps the harbormaster's duplicates, begin building a paper chain: manifests, coal tallies, his own light log proving the shoal was marked. The old pilot teaches them the coves in case a boat is needed. Emotional beat: quiet, obsessive hope; two careful people learning to trust.

chapters.title: The Historian Arrives Early
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Before the thaw, the Admiralty sends its own chronicler, Mr. Quill-Harrow, a polite, patient man who interviews Mirabel over tea and clearly already knows about the satchel. Emotional beat: the chill of being seen at last; Mirabel understands the race has already started.

chapters.title: What Ede Would Say
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, interleaved with memory of Ede, who once testified against a shipping magnate and lost everything for it. He rages at her ghost for the ruin her courage cost them — and hears her answer: the ruin came from the silence after, not the speaking. Emotional beat: the thematic heart; grief reframed as inheritance.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Coal Store
chapters.summary: Cook's POV. The disgraced cook, desperate for reinstatement, signals Quill-Harrow's launch. The tower is searched; the satchel's hiding place is nearly found; Nell hides the papers inside the lamp mechanism itself. Emotional beat: the found family fractures and, in the crisis, chooses each other anyway.

chapters.title: The Cook's Confession
chapters.summary: Cook's POV. Caught between shame and the pilot's unexpected mercy, the cook confesses to the household — and reveals Quill-Harrow's deadline: the official history will be sealed the day the bridge reopens. Emotional beat: forgiveness as strategy; the enemy's clock becomes their own.

chapters.title: Storm Season, Deepening
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. A two-week blizzard traps everyone together; stores run low; Mirabel and Nell keep the light burning through ice-fouled glass in shifts that become a ritual. Emotional beat: hardship as bonding; the tower becomes a home rather than a hiding place.

chapters.title: Tamsin's Duplicates
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She reveals she has risked everything for years quietly copying the harbormaster's true ledgers, waiting for someone with the nerve to use them. Mirabel finally stops being invisible by being known. Emotional beat: two loners recognizing each other; love arriving without announcement.

chapters.title: The Pilot's Route
chapters.summary: Pilot's POV. The old smuggler charts a run to the mainland newspaper town before the bridge opens — through the worst shoals, in a boat that barely floats. Mirabel must decide whether the papers leave or whether he does. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal; choosing the record over the self.

chapters.title: Quill-Harrow's Offer
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Quill-Harrow returns with an offer: silence and the satchel in exchange for Mirabel's pension, his post, and Nell's passage to her aunt's — a comfortable, erased life. Emotional beat: the seduction of safety; Mirabel nearly takes it, and the reader understands why.

chapters.title: Nell at the Lamp
chapters.summary: Nell's POV. Nell confronts Mirabel: her father died carrying the truth and Mirabel would trade it for a warm room. She lights the lamp alone through a gale to show him what keeping a light actually means. Emotional beat: fury as love; Mirabel's decision crystallizes in her defiance.

chapters.title: The Run Through the Shoals
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Before dawn on the last storm night, Mirabel, Tamsin, and the pilot run the coves with the papers, pursued by Quill-Harrow's launch through fog and breaking seas. Mirabel's light log, his arithmetic, his whole careful life becomes navigation. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into competence; the keeper finally steers his own course.

chapters.title: The Bridge Opens
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, then Quill-Harrow's briefly. The thaw comes; the first official crossing brings the historians in force — and a journalist Mirabel's papers reached hours earlier. The inquiry cannot be sealed; the truth is on the record. Emotional beat: triumph with no music in it; victory measured in ink, not applause.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. He loses the post, the pension, and the light — and packs to leave carrying almost nothing, discovering how little of his life was ever in the stores. The harbor households refuse to let him go alone. Emotional beat: loss and fullness in the same breath; the ledger finally balanced.

chapters.title: Mara and the Harbor
chapters.summary: Nell's POV, one year later. A new light burns on the point, tended by a small found family; Nell, apprenticed as an assistant keeper, logs the first entry in a fresh book and names the light for her father's last word to her. Mirabel, no longer invisible, signs his full name beneath hers. Emotional beat: the price paid, the family kept, the light still burning.
